claims.text: Mechanical alloying of HfMoTaTiZr will produce a metastable single-phase solid solution.
Mechanically alloyed HfMoTaTiZr will have higher room-temperature yield strength than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Mechanically alloyed HfMoTaTiZr will have higher yield strength at temperatures up to 1000 °C than the as-cast alloy.
Mechanically alloyed HfMoTaTiZr will have higher fracture toughness than the as-cast alloy.
Mechanical alloying without a stated compositional change will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Solid-solution strengthening will contribute to the improved mechanical performance of HfMoTaTiZr.
Secondary-phase precipitation may occur in the proposed mechanically alloyed HfMoTaTiZr.
Secondary-phase precipitation may strengthen the proposed alloy.
Dislocation slip will govern or contribute to the mechanical response of mechanically alloyed HfMoTaTiZr.
Twinning may govern or contribute to the mechanical response of mechanically alloyed HfMoTaTiZr.
The activity of dislocation slip and possible twinning is influenced by alloy microstructure and composition.
Mechanical alloying may produce a non-uniform HfMoTaTiZr microstructure that affects its properties.
Mechanical properties will be evaluated at room temperature and at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C under tensile and compressive loading.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is the baseline for evaluating the intervention.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as producing a single-phase solid solution, while the proposed mediator includes precipitation of secondary phases. These states could occur sequentially, but no thermal history or phase-evolution sequence is given to reconcile them.
